s: baby chick blender (machine that kills unwanted chicks in egg-producing facilities)
chick (young bird), fledgling, hatchling, squab (of a pigeon or dove)
Küken.et: Via German Low German from Middle Low German kuken, from Old Saxon *kiukīn, from Proto-West Germanic *kiukīn (“chicken”). Cognate with Dutch kuiken, English chicken. A related form is Middle High German kuchil, whence now obsolete Küchlein.

Kukuruz.et:
Attested from 1697. From Serbo-Croatian kukuruz or Romanian cucuruz (see there for further etymology).
Compare Russian кукуруза (kukuruza), Hungarian kukorica, Slovene koruza, Polish kukurydza, etc.

s: imperial and royal, (with reference to the Habsburg monarchy), K and K
k. u. k..et: Abbreviation of kaiserlich und königlich (Imperial and Royal).
